name: Environmental Studies
notes: Designed to link natural and social sciences for students interested in environmental management.
If more than two intermediate core courses are taken, the extras count as technical electives; likewise for extra skills courses.

The five elective courses must form a coherent program agreed with the faculty advisors, drawn from two groups (natural sciences and engineering; social sciences/humanities). The page does not enumerate them here, so they are modeled as related 200-level courses across both groups - NEEDS VERIFICATION against the department's elective lists.
One additional 100-level EESC course may count as a technical elective if taken in the first year.
STAT 180 is the current number for the former STAT 212; the page also lists STAT 211.

requirementGroups.label: Chemistry
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Chemistry: CHEM 131: Chemical Concepts, Systems, and Practices I

requirementGroups.label: Mathematics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Mathematics: (choose one of the following options) MATH 161: Calculus IA; MATH 141: Calculus I and MATH 142: Calculus II

requirementGroups.label: Introductory core course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose one of the following introductory core courses: EESC 100: Introduction to Oceanography; EESC 101: Introduction to Earth Sciences; EESC 103: Introduction to Environmental Science; EESC 105: Introduction to Climate Change

requirementGroups.label: Intermediate core courses (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose two of the following: EESC 201: Evolution of the Earth; EESC 212: A Climate Change Perspective to Chemical Oceanography; EESC 213(W): Hydrology and Water Resources; EESC 216(W): Environmental Geochemistry; EESC 218: Atmospheric Geochemistry; EESC 219: Energy and Society; EESC 223: Earth Surface Processes; EESC 235: Physical Oceanography; EESC 236(W): Physics of Climate

requirementGroups.label: Skills course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose one of the following: CHEM 203/207: Organic Chemistry plus Lab; CSC 161: Introduction to Programming; EESC 214: Earth Science Data Analysis; EESC 221: Quantitative Environmental Problem Solving; EESC 251: Introduction to GIS; STAT 211: Applied Statistics for the Social Sciences; STAT 180: Introduction to Applied Statistical Methodology
requirementGroups.note: The CHEM 203 route also requires the CHEM 207 lab.

requirementGroups.label: Elective courses (5)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Five elective courses must be chosen to create what the student and the faculty advisors view as a coherent program. The elective courses are presented in two groups: Natural sciences and engineering; Social sciences/humanities
requirementGroups.note: NEEDS VERIFICATION - the per-group elective lists are not on this page.

upperLevelWriting.label: Two upper-level writing courses within the major
upperLevelWriting.note: NEEDS VERIFICATION: the page states no explicit ULW policy; modeled as the College's two-course norm satisfied by the department's W courses (EESC 213W, 216W, 236W and others exist in the catalog).
